Simon, Evelyn —

Quick technical note (high level) based on the usage extract you provided. Will expand for the follow-up doc but wanted to get practical guidance in time for the call.

1) Quantization recommendations
- Chat/LLM generation (diverse prompts, fidelity matters): Q4_0 (4-bit FP mapping) for ~2–4% average nll/quality degradation vs FP16 for most open models; INT8 is riskier for hallucination-sensitive outputs.
- Embeddings: INT8 usually safe for cosine similarity workloads and gives ~2–3x memory reduction; recommend running a 1k-sample embedding quality check.
- Suggested split: keep generation models at Q4_0 by default, embed models at INT8 for batch-heavy flows.

2) Batching & KV cache policy
- Short-chat (latency-sensitive): small max batch size (8–16), aggressive 0ms batching window, prioritized routing to low-latency pools. Prefix KV caching off for user-turns requiring up-to-date context; prefix caching on for system-level tokens to reduce compute.
- Long-form summarization: larger batch sizes (64–128) with a slightly higher batching window (10–30ms) to improve throughput — move to dedicated burst pool if p95 < 2s is required.

3) Cost impact (rough estimates)
- Moving embeddings to INT8: ~30–40% token compute cost reduction on heavy embedding workloads (depends on kernel support and sequence length).
- Q4_0 for generation: ~20–30% cost reduction vs FP16 at similar latency for moderate sequence lengths (<=1024).
- Batching changes can reduce per-token cost by 15–50% depending on steady-state QPS and tail latency SLOs.

4) Commercial packaging suggestions
- Pilot: 3 months, $20k in pilot credits (usable across hosted/dedicated) + technical onboarding.
- Committed credits: tiered discounts at 10%/15%/22% for 6/12/24 month commits respectively (higher for larger commits).
- Optimize Add-on (paid): includes customized batching presets and priority model-variant routing for production-critical flows.

Next technical steps for us to finalize numbers:
- A 1k-sample embedding quality check (we can run)
- Clarify percentage of requests that are low-latency vs throughput-first
- Confirm preferred model family(s) (e.g., LlamaX / Redstone family)

I’ll prepare the 2-page technical note and include a sample pricing sheet with delta scenarios by Friday.

—Diego
Diego Fernandez
Sr. Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
